description: Figure 9 presents a grouped bar chart titled “Comprehensive Evaluation Results on Academic and Practical Benchmarks,” comparing the performance of four models across nine different datasets and evaluation metrics. The vertical axis, labeled “Score (%)”, ranges from 0 to 80 in increments of 10. The horizontal axis lists the datasets: GSM-8K, MMLU, HumanEval, TruthfulQA, ARC, MBPP, LC AlpacaEval-2, MT-Bench (×5), and Chat-Arena-Hard. Each dataset has four adjacent bars representing: LLaMA-3-8B-it (blue), Ours (SFT baseline) (orange), Ours (DPO baseline) (green), and Ours (Iterative RLHF) (red), as indicated in the legend. Performance varies across benchmarks: on GSM-8K, all models score above 70%, with Ours (Iterative RLHF) reaching approximately 80%. On MMLU and HumanEval, scores cluster between 60–65%. TruthfulQA shows lower scores overall, with LLaMA-3-8B-it at ~44% and Ours (Iterative RLHF) at ~60%. ARC and MBPP show moderate performance (~60–65%). LC AlpacaEval-2 shows a sharp drop, with LLaMA-3-8B-it at ~23%, SFT baseline at ~10%, DPO at ~22%, and Iterative RLHF at ~31%. MT-Bench (×5) scores range from ~38% to ~42%, and Chat-Arena-Hard shows the lowest scores, with LLaMA-3-8B-it at ~20%, SFT at ~5%, DPO at ~22%, and Iterative RLHF at ~29%. The chart visually emphasizes that the “Ours (Iterative RLHF)” model generally outperforms the others across most benchmarks, particularly on more challenging or practical datasets.
